position: Upright standing, arms resting at the sides. Read the space between the feet from the source image rather than a modern template.
transition: Preparation is the starting reference for Opening; the still does not show the arms rising.
application: Study a balanced base from which direction can change. This is an interpretive exercise, not a photographed partner technique.
attention: Notice contact beneath both feet without making the knees rigid.
name_context: Wu Chi is the wording in the supplied list; the historical source presents a preparatory standing posture.

position: The archive has standing endpoints but no separate montage image of the moving opening.
transition: The change from rest to the first ward-off must be read as movement between pictures, not recovered from one frame.
application: Consider how the arms can lift without lifting the shoulders. A still cannot establish an application by itself.
attention: Let attention widen to the whole body before following a hand.
name_context: The absence of an Opening panel is a feature of this montage, not evidence that the action was absent from practice.

position: Rounded arms change relationship across ward-off, rollback, press and push. Some occurrences retain only one of these phases.
transition: Follow the changes of weight and the turning of the trunk across the image sequence.
application: Compare receiving, redirecting and returning pressure as different tasks; these are study interpretations, not a single fixed use.
attention: Keep awareness of the rear foot while looking at the hands.
name_context: Bird and sparrow are alternative English wordings in the supplied list. They do not establish different styles.

position: One hand forms a hook while the opposite palm extends, with the feet separated into a broad stance.
transition: Track the turn into the open shape; do not treat the hook as an isolated gesture.
application: The two arms can be studied as separating or controlling lines of contact. The solo plate does not specify a partner's position.
attention: Allow the elbows to retain shape without locking them.
name_context: The repeated Single Whips help locate the intervening sequences in the long form.

position: The familiar hook and open palm appear on a different line through the floor.
transition: Read the changed direction in relation to the preceding Embrace the Tiger and the following Parting Mane.
application: Explore the same two-arm relationship on a diagonal rather than assuming a new hand technique.
attention: Track the direction of the feet as well as that of the extended palm.
name_context: Diagonal identifies this occurrence in the supplied modern sequence.

position: The hands face towards each other at different heights, with the forward foot lightly placed.
transition: Notice the narrowing of the stance after Single Whip and the subsequent opening into White Crane.
application: The converging arms suggest a study of receiving between two contact points; this is an interpretation of the shape.
attention: Avoid making the arms tense merely to hold their outline.
name_context: The name includes a step, although the montage records only its terminal position.

position: One hand is high and the other low, with the front foot lightly placed.
transition: Compare how the raised hand can descend as the next Brush Knee begins.
application: The contrasting arm heights offer a study of separating upper and lower lines of contact.
attention: Notice the length of the upright trunk without raising the shoulders.
name_context: The bird name is imagery attached to the posture; this catalogue does not claim an animal-origin story.

position: The left hand is low beside the leading knee while the opposite palm reaches forward.
transition: Compare the front foot placement and trunk direction before attending to the reaching hand.
application: Study simultaneous clearing with one hand and forward contact with the other; no single target is prescribed here.
attention: Let the forward hand and the change of weight remain part of one action.
name_context: Left names the side of the brushing action in this catalogue.

position: The right hand is low beside the leading knee while the opposite palm reaches forward.
transition: Compare this side with the neighbouring left version, allowing for the changed camera view.
application: Study the relationship between clearing a low line and extending the opposite palm.
attention: Keep awareness of both feet during the side change.
name_context: A rear view of the right version is not evidence that the source image was mirrored.

position: Both hands gather in front, the forward foot light and the weight drawn back.
transition: The narrowing from Brush Knee is visible in the change of stance; the intermediate hand path is not fully recorded.
application: The two hands can be studied as coordinated contact points along an arm. This is an interpretive possibility.
attention: Notice the space between the hands without squeezing it shut.
name_context: The instrument name describes a recognisable arrangement; it is not evidence of a literal playing motion.

position: A fist extends from a stepped stance in the endpoint images. Some montage occurrences instead show the preceding parry.
transition: Use the historical sequences to distinguish the turn, step, parry and final extension.
application: Study clearing a path before the fist travels forward. An isolated punch photograph omits that preparation.
attention: Follow the relationship between the rear foot, trunk and fist rather than reaching from the shoulder alone.
name_context: The compound English name covers several actions, so a single plate may not show its named finish.

position: Both open hands finish in front after the preceding fist action.
transition: Compare the gathering phase and renewed forward extension in Chen's sequence.
application: Releasing or changing an existing contact provides one possible study of the withdrawal and return.
attention: Keep attention through the retreat as well as the forward phase.
name_context: Apparent Close Up occurs at section endings but is followed by further movement.

position: The forearms cross in front as the feet come into a more square relationship.
transition: This gathering marks a section boundary; the later final occurrence is not separately drawn in the montage.
application: Crossing can be explored as receiving and reorganising the arms, without assuming a fixed block.
attention: Notice the whole stance settling, not only the crossing wrists.
name_context: Repeated section boundaries explain why this image appears at several places in the catalogue.

position: A turn leads into a sequence that includes rollback, press and push; the montage sometimes gives several panels.
transition: Treat this as a compound passage rather than assigning a new movement number to every frame.
application: Study receiving from a changed direction and recovering a forward line of contact.
attention: Keep the turn connected to the feet instead of twisting the shoulders alone.
name_context: The tiger and mountain wording is preserved as a traditional title, without an asserted origin legend.

position: A low fist sits beneath the opposite elbow while the forward foot is lightly placed.
transition: Compare the narrowing from the previous larger arm pattern before the retreating steps begin.
application: The arrangement can suggest paired control and striking lines; the solo image does not establish their exact use.
attention: Notice the relationship between the upper elbow and lower fist without compressing the chest.
name_context: The title describes the conspicuous relationship between the two arms.

position: One hand reaches forward while the other withdraws; the sequence travels backwards.
transition: Compare consecutive side changes, not just the forward-facing palm.
application: Retreat with maintained contact is a useful interpretive theme; withdrawing need not mean abandoning the forward line.
attention: Attend to the landing foot before transferring weight to it.
name_context: Side labels vary between sources: an advancing hand and a retreating leg can name the same phase differently.

position: The opposite hand-and-foot arrangement continues the retreating series.
transition: Follow the alternation with the left-labelled occurrence while retaining the backward travel.
application: Study changing the receiving and returning roles of the hands during a retreat.
attention: Keep attention on the space behind the stepping foot as well as in front.
name_context: The repeated series is condensed in the montage; reused images are labelled explicitly.

position: The arms open along a diagonal, with the trunk and stance turned from the preceding retreat.
transition: Observe how the outward arm and step develop together into a wider shape.
application: An opening across a contact line is one possible reading; the photograph cannot determine the opponent's placement.
attention: Notice the connection across the back between the two arms.
name_context: Diagonal Flying is a posture title, not a claim that the body leaves the ground.

position: The trunk inclines and one hand reaches down towards the floor.
transition: Compare the lowered reach with the following upward and forward opening of Fan Through the Back.
application: A downward redirection is a possible study theme; depth in an old photograph is not a required modern range.
attention: Keep attention on the supporting legs while the hand lowers.
name_context: Sea-bottom imagery names the downward reach; no literal depth or origin story is implied.

position: One hand extends forward while the other shelters high beside the head.
transition: The source sequence places this opening after Needle and before a turning action.
application: Study simultaneous protection above and extension ahead as an interpretation of the two-arm shape.
attention: Notice the width across the back without stiffening the shoulders.
name_context: Fan Through the Back is retained as supplied; English translations of this name differ.

position: Two plates show a turning action and a fist-led continuation.
transition: Compare the before-and-after body directions; a single frame cannot recover the full turn.
application: A turning deflection followed by contact is a possible study of the sequence.
attention: Keep the gaze and feet involved in the turn rather than forcing the neck.
name_context: Chen names a corresponding later passage differently; those images are not silently treated as identical.

position: The rounded arms exchange upper and lower positions while the stance moves sideways.
transition: The montage uses one representative image for each three-entry series; it does not depict all three cycles.
application: Study alternating contact and redirection while changing the base sideways.
attention: Attend to the moment one foot becomes free to move.
name_context: The cloud image is a movement metaphor. A still records a phase, not the complete repeated pattern.

position: A high palm extends while the body gathers back over its support.
transition: Compare the withdrawal and reaching action before the kick preparation.
application: A high receiving or checking contact is one possible interpretation of the hand position.
attention: Keep the reaching palm soft enough that the shoulder need not rise.
name_context: The horse title is preserved without adding an unverified riding anecdote.

position: The right leg lifts and extends while the hands open apart.
transition: Read the preparation and kick as separate phases; the montage supplies both here.
application: The hands and lifted leg suggest simultaneous upper contact and a lower action; exact targets remain interpretive.
attention: Notice balance on the standing leg instead of pursuing height.
name_context: Separation Kick is distinguished from Heel Kick in the supplied sequence.

position: The left leg lifts and extends while the hands open apart.
transition: Compare the landing and reorganisation from the preceding right kick before the left leg rises.
application: Study how upper-body contact and a free leg might coexist without leaning to reach.
attention: Let attention remain on the standing foot while the other leg moves.
name_context: The separate preparation image helps prevent a lifted-knee frame being mistaken for the finished kick.

position: The left leg extends with the heel presented; the body may face away from the camera after a turn.
transition: The still captures the extended leg, not the complete turning or landing path.
application: A heel-led pushing action is an interpretive reading of the foot shape.
attention: Keep breathing easy while balancing; do not use breath-holding to maintain the pose.
name_context: Left identifies the kicking leg here, unlike the standing-leg convention used for Golden Rooster.

position: The right leg extends with the heel presented and the arms separated.
transition: Check the preceding entry to distinguish this repeated endpoint from the different turns that lead to it.
application: Study a heel-led action with the arms maintaining spatial awareness.
attention: Notice unnecessary tension in the jaw and shoulders during single-leg balance.
name_context: Repeated right heel kicks are different occurrences of a related posture, not duplicate catalogue errors.

position: The fist angles down from a forward stance and the trunk inclines with it.
transition: Compare the preceding Brush Knee and the following turn to locate this low punch.
application: A descending line of contact is visible; a particular target is not recoverable from the solo plate alone.
attention: Follow the diagonal through the whole body rather than folding only at the neck.
name_context: This entry remains separate from the later Punch Groin despite their visual resemblance.

position: The arms form a high and low pair of fists, with the left-oriented stance seen largely from behind.
transition: The next Tiger posture changes side; compare the feet to understand the change of direction.
application: The paired levels offer a study of protecting one line while acting on another.
attention: Notice that both arms belong to one turned trunk.
name_context: Tiger names are shared across different postures and do not by themselves prove identical mechanics.

position: One fist is high beside the head while the other occupies a lower line in the opposite orientation.
transition: Read the shift from the preceding left Tiger before the next heel kick.
application: Study the relationship of upper cover and lower contact as an editorial interpretation.
attention: Avoid drawing the high shoulder up towards the ear.
name_context: The paired left and right entries are retained separately, including their differing camera views.

position: Both fists approach from the sides at approximately head height.
transition: The posture follows a heel kick; the landing and gathering are part of the transition, not shown by the endpoint alone.
application: The name suggests paired head-level strikes. The archive records solo form rather than a demonstration on a partner.
attention: Attend to the roundness of the arms without clenching the shoulders.
name_context: The explicit target belongs to the supplied historical-style name; it is not a training recommendation.

position: The arms separate diagonally as the right-leading stance opens.
transition: The alternating steps continue the same family; the montage reuses its right-side image for the third entry.
application: The separated arms suggest opening through or around a line of contact.
attention: Notice the lower hand as well as the more conspicuous raised arm.
name_context: The horse-mane title supplies imagery, but the archive does not establish an origin tale.

position: The diagonal separation appears on the opposite side in a left-leading stance.
transition: Compare its foot and trunk changes with the right-side occurrences on either side.
application: Study the same opening relationship with the hands exchanging roles.
attention: Let attention include the supporting foot during the change of side.
name_context: Left and right versions are related shapes, not licence to mirror the historical photographs.

position: One forearm rises above the head while the other hand extends; four plates show changing corners.
transition: Follow the four images in order. They belong to one numbered entry in the supplied list.
application: Upper receiving and forward contact offer an interpretive theme across changes of direction.
attention: Re-establish the feet and gaze at each corner instead of following only the hands.
name_context: The weaving title is retained; this catalogue does not infer a literal loom mechanism from the name.

position: The body lowers into a long stance, with one arm reaching along the lower line.
transition: The first occurrence leads to Golden Rooster; the second leads to Seven Stars.
application: Changing level while maintaining contact is one possible interpretation of the low shape.
attention: Use the photograph to observe relationships, not to demand its depth from your own joints.
name_context: The same low posture has different continuations at its two locations in the sequence.

position: The left leg supports the body while the right knee and corresponding hand rise.
transition: The body gathers upwards from the low posture into a single-leg balance.
application: The lifted knee and hand suggest coordinated close-range actions; their partner context is not photographed here.
attention: Keep attention on the standing foot and an easy upright balance.
name_context: The supplied list names the standing leg. The 1931 source instead names this posture by the raised side.

position: The right leg supports the body while the left knee and corresponding hand rise.
transition: The support changes sides before the sequence returns to retreating steps.
application: Study the coordination of the lifted knee and hand as a relationship rather than an isolated high knee.
attention: Notice whether changing support produces unnecessary breath-holding.
name_context: Chen's caption and image filename disagree in this pair; the catalogue follows the caption and visible leg position.

position: A turning sequence ends with an open hand rather than the earlier fist-led continuation.
transition: Compare the two phases and their position late in the sequence; Chen's named comparison occurs earlier.
application: An open-hand continuation after a turn can be explored without claiming identical mechanics across the manuals.
attention: Notice the change of hand form while keeping the trunk's turn connected.
name_context: The snake title is attested in these sources; its placement and execution are not identical across them.

position: The High Pat family continues into a further palm reach.
transition: Follow the continuation beyond the earlier High Pat endpoint before the Cross Kick.
application: A reaching contact after gathering is a possible study of the extended action.
attention: Let the eyes follow the intended direction without pushing the head forwards.
name_context: The added Palm Thrust wording distinguishes this occurrence from the earlier High Pat.

position: The raised leg crosses the body's line while the upper body organises a corresponding hand action.
transition: A single image cannot establish the complete leg path. Yang and Chen show related but differing versions.
application: Compare an instep or slapping action with Chen's pressing-kick description; do not collapse them into one technique.
attention: Keep awareness of the supporting foot during the crossing action.
name_context: This is explicitly catalogued as a historical variant comparison, not an exact match between manuals.

position: A low forward fist follows the kick, with the body directed along the stepping line.
transition: Its late placement after Cross Kick distinguishes it from the earlier downward punch.
application: The supplied title names a low target; the image alone establishes only the solo position.
attention: Keep attention on the path into the stance rather than only the final fist.
name_context: Punch Groin is retained as the supplied name, without turning a solo archival image into partner instruction.

position: The fists cross in front and the forward foot is lightly placed.
transition: The body rises from the low posture, then withdraws into Ride the Tiger.
application: The crossed arms offer a study of gathering or receiving along two lines.
attention: Notice the change from the long low base to the smaller upright one.
name_context: Seven Stars is a traditional title; no unverified astronomical or anatomical explanation is assigned here.

position: One hand rises and the other lowers while the weight gathers back.
transition: Its place between Seven Stars and Lotus identifies this occurrence despite its resemblance to White Crane.
application: The contrast between upper and lower contact lines offers one interpretive study.
attention: Attend to the withdrawal through the feet rather than leaning the trunk back.
name_context: A similar silhouette does not make this the same named movement as White Crane.

position: The leg is lifted with the hands gathered near its path.
transition: The photograph captures a phase of the circular kick, not its complete sweep or landing.
application: A sweeping leg action with coordinated hands is a possible reading; the still cannot specify timing.
attention: Follow balance and orientation rather than trying to reproduce a high kick from a photograph.
name_context: Lotus supplies the movement's title; a flower analogy does not establish an exact trajectory.

position: The fists occupy separated lines in a turned stance after the Lotus action.
transition: Compare the feet after the kick and before the final advancing punch.
application: The opposed arm positions suggest paired control and striking possibilities; these remain interpretations.
attention: Notice the connection across the back without exaggerating the pull of the arms.
name_context: The bow title evokes opposing actions; the historical photo is not a literal archery demonstration.

position: The montage preserves a standing endpoint rather than a separate view of the lowering arms.
transition: Read Closing after the final Cross Hands, which is also omitted as a distinct final montage frame.
application: Study the return from an active shape to resting alignment rather than assigning a speculative combat use.
attention: Let attention broaden as the hands settle.
name_context: Closing and Return share a final photograph; they are still separate entries in the supplied list.

position: Standing at rest completes the sequence, using the same terminal image as Closing.
transition: This is the endpoint of the form, with no further pose inferred from the archive.
application: The useful study here is recovery of balance and quiet standing.
attention: Notice the feet, hands and breath without imposing a special finishing breath.
name_context: Return to Wu Chi is the supplied wording for the final entry.
